name: Rechargeable hydrogen oil tank
effect: nickel adds hydrogen to liquid carrier oils
how: Hydrogen gas is hard to store, so a nickel catalyst instead bonds it onto an oily liquid, the same trick that hardens vegetable oil into margarine. The loaded oil sits in an ordinary steel tank at normal pressure like diesel. When energy is needed, heating it over a catalyst releases the hydrogen and the empty oil is reused.
why: Margarine chemistry turned into a safe, pumpable hydrogen tank.
real: liquid organic hydrogen carriers, pilot plants 2010s
